expectations.text: Proposes a specific, curiosity-driving subject line rather than a flat 'DeltaHack and Brannock Systems partnership'-style label
expectations.evidence: The proposed subject is 'Hands-on feedback on your tracing agent from 500 student builders'. It is specific: it names her product, a concrete number and the value on offer. It is clearly not a flat partnership label. It's more a value statement than a curiosity hook, and there is no open loop or question, so it falls just short of a full score.

expectations.text: Proposes a specific, curiosity-driving subject line rather than a flat 'DeltaHack and Brannock Systems partnership'-style label
expectations.evidence: The subject line is "tracing agent feedback". It is short, lowercase and specific. It points to Lena's own public request for feedback on Brannock's new tracing agent, not to a generic sponsorship or partnership. That makes it relevant to her and likely to get opened, and it avoids the flat partnership-label pattern. Curiosity is only moderate: it names a topic and gives no hook such as the 500 student developers. Only one option is offered, with no alternatives and no reasoning for the choice, so it falls short of a full 5.
